title: Protein-mediated stabilization and nicking of the non-template DNA strand dramatically affect R-loop formation in vitro
authors: Ethan Holleman; Thomas E. Catley; Tadas Sereiva; Stella R. Hartono; Alice L.B. Pyne; Frédéric Chédin
one_liner_zh: 该文研究单链DNA结合蛋白和DNA切口对R-loop形成的体外调控，涉及蛋白-DNA互作但非TF-DNA体系，且方法以实验和AFM为主，无AI或物理模拟建模，与课题方法轴不匹配。
abstract: R-loops are an important class of non-B DNA structures that form co-transcriptionally. Using in vitro transcription and unbiased quantitative sequencing readouts, we show that the addition of single-strand DNA binding proteins co-transcriptionally can drive a 3- to 5-fold increase of R-loop frequency without significant changes to R-loop distribution. We propose that this is caused by stabilizing and preventing the collapse of short nascent R-loops. This suggests that R-loop formation is highly dynamic and highlights single strand binding proteins as players in cellular R-loop regulation. We further show that non-template strand DNA nicks are powerful initiators of R-loop formation, increasing R-loop frequencies by up to two orders of magnitude. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) revealed that the non-template strand in nick-initiated structures is often flayed away from the RNA:DNA hybrid and engaged in self-pairing, creating unique forked R-loop features. DNA nicks, one of the most frequent DNA lesions in cells, are therefore potential hotspots for opportunistic R-loop initiation and may cause the formation of a novel class of R-loops. Overall, this work highlights the importance of the displaced single-strand on R-loop initiation and dynamics. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT R-loops are three-stranded DNA:RNA hybrid structures that form during transcription and play critical roles in both gene regulation and genome stability. This study reveals that single-stranded DNA-binding protein (SSB) increases R-loop frequency by stabilizing nascent R-loops, revealing a role for this protein in R-loop dynamics. Additionally, single strand DNA breaks, common cellular lesions, are identified as potent initiators of R-loops, increasing their rate of formation by up to 100-fold. Using atomic force microscopy, the study uncovers unique forked structures in nick-initiated R-loops, representing a novel class of secondary R-loop structures. These findings provide new insights into how cellular factors and DNA damage influence R-loop formation, with implications for understanding genome instability in health and disease.
abstract_zh: R-loops是一类重要的非B型DNA结构，在共转录过程中形成。通过体外转录和无偏定量测序读数，我们展示了在共转录过程中添加单链DNA结合蛋白可使R-loop频率增加3至5倍，而R-loop分布无显著变化。我们提出这归因于稳定并防止短新生R-loops的塌缩。这表明R-loop形成高度动态，并突出单链结合蛋白在细胞R-loop调控中的作用。我们进一步展示非模板链DNA切口是R-loop形成的强效启动因子，可将R-loop频率提高至两个数量级。原子力显微镜（AFM）揭示，在切口启动的结构中，非模板链常从RNA:DNA杂交体上剥离并参与自配对，形成独特的叉状R-loop特征。DNA切口作为细胞中最常见的DNA损伤之一，因此可能是机会性R-loop启动的潜在热点，并可能导致一类新型R-loops的形成。总体而言，这项工作强调了被置换的单链在R-loop启动和动态中的重要性。意义声明 R-loops是在转录过程中形成的三链DNA:RNA杂交结构，在基因调控和基因组稳定性中均发挥关键作用。本研究揭示单链DNA结合蛋白（SSB）通过稳定新生R-loops增加其频率，揭示了该蛋白在R-loop动态中的作用。此外，单链DNA断裂作为常见的细胞损伤，被鉴定为R-loops的强效启动因子，将其形成速率提高至100倍。利用原子力显微镜，研究揭示了切口启动的R-loops中独特的叉状结构，代表了一类新型次级R-loop结构。这些发现为细胞因子和DNA损伤如何影响R-loop形成提供了新见解，对理解健康和疾病中的基因组不稳定性具有重要意义。
